matrix: Ready-to-eat baked breakfast cereal bar; potato-derived distarch phosphate, VERSAFIBE 1490. Recipe, bake conditions and actual portion masses were not recovered.
design: Randomized participant-blinded single-center crossover, 31 healthy adults.
matching: Original publication abstract describes matching energy, available carbohydrate and sugars; actual per-arm grams unavailable.
label_caveat: Arm labels do not establish analytical total fiber for a consumed portion.

sampling.published: Serial blood collection over two hours; exact actual times not in abstract.

outcomes.current_registration: Positive glucose iAUC primary. Insulin positive iAUC, peak and net iAUC secondary under detailedDescription. Original version wording unverified. First submitted Feb 5 2019; started Feb 11; first publicly posted Feb 18; primary completion October 25.
outcomes.observed_publication: Abstract reports P > 0.05 for insulin iAUC across tested doses; does not provide native arm estimates, paired contrasts, ranking, interval, units, or positive/net implementation.

acquisition: Publisher HTML led to unauthenticated abstract; PDF and graphical abstract could not be recovered. OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and Unpaywall had no open version. DataCite related-DOI and Figshare resource-DOI searches returned no records. Searched IIT/ProQuest, conference and post-completion regulatory deposits; no verified arm table or figure. Ingredion submission FDA-2016-N-3389-0423 dated Feb 13 2017 predates trial. No author contact or access agreement.

secondary_context_only.finding: Overlapping investigators described the two active arms as delivering 10 and 20 g potato fiber; also report matching available carbohydrate, fat and protein. No arm-specific grams of available carbohydrate or native insulin means.
Later authors describe Du as adding RS4 atop the control formulation. Their general remark on testing at 50 g includes multiple references and is insufficient to assign per-arm doses.
